gloss: to be taught, to learn from

definitions.gloss: to be taught, to learn from
definitions.explanation: To receive instruction or knowledge from someone.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}に{日本語|にほんご}を{教|おそ}わった。
examples.english: I was taught Japanese by my teacher.

examples.japanese: {母|はは}に{料理|りょうり}を{教|おそ}わる。
examples.english: I learn cooking from my mother.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}から{多|おお}くのことを{教|おそ}わった。
examples.english: I learned many things from him.

examples.japanese: {友達|ともだち}にギターの{弾|ひ}き{方|かた}を{教|おそ}わった。
examples.english: I learned how to play guitar from a friend.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}の{頃|ころ}、{祖母|そぼ}に{編|あ}み{物|もの}を{教|おそ}わったことを{今|いま}でも{覚|おぼ}えている。
examples.english: I still remember being taught knitting by my grandmother when I was a child.

notes:
{教|おそ}わる is an intransitive godan verb meaning 'to be taught' or 'to learn from someone.'

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: {自動詞|じどうし} (intransitive)
- Pair: {教|おし}える (transitive, to teach)

PATTERN:
[person]に [subject]を {教|おそ}わる = to learn [subject] from [person]

EXAMPLES:
- {先生|せんせい}に{日本語|にほんご}を{教|おそ}わる: to learn Japanese from a teacher
- {母|はは}に{料理|りょうり}を{教|おそ}わった: I learned cooking from my mother
- {彼|かれ}から{多|おお}くを{教|おそ}わった: I learned a lot from him

CONTRAST WITH {習|なら}う:
- {教|おそ}わる emphasizes receiving instruction from someone
- {習|なら}う is more general 'to learn/take lessons'

Both use the pattern [person]に...を, but {教|おそ}わる highlights the teaching relationship.
